Some of the elements, key elements, of the preparation to which I will draw your attention, apart from identifying appropriate candidates for certain particular tasks, also involve ensuring contact, preparations for taking over control of security service centres and also involvement, contacts with public security service centres in certain areas, the principal one I believe was in Banja Luka, although there was one in the principal towns in each of the other four autonomous regions. Also, part of this preparation was ensuring preparations with regard to active and reserve members of the police forces, the Territorial and Defence Force and Civil Defence units so that they would be in a position to have adequate numbers in place at whatever time it would be appropriate. Finally, for this part of it I think I can indicate the intention throughout to co-operate with units of the JNA. In particular, I draw your attention to the point here, which the instruction is to begin equipping war-time units with personnel, military resources and livestock reserves according to JNA designations.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Dr. Gow, what is the date of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I already gave the date which was 19th December 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. Dr. Gow, was this activity by the Bosnian Serbs and the activity by the JNA brought about as a consequence of provocation, be it fabricated or genuine, in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As you put the question, I would have to answer it on two levels. Certainly, on a broad level, there was a process of action and reaction in Bosnia and Herzegovina. I believe that members of the Serbian communities in Bosnia and Herzegovina, as per some of the documents and declarations we have seen, would regard the declaration of sovereignty and the declaration of independence as being a provocative act. On another level, with regard to operational questions and activities in specific areas, it is clear that as part of a pattern of activities in a number of places such as Bijeljina, such as Zvornik, there was what appears to be an act of provocation within the town which provided the justification for action by the JNA which had artillery placed usually outside the town and by paramilitary forces which would enter the town, again according to the pattern I identified in testimony yesterday with regard to Croatia, that is, the JNA providing the heavier weaponry but not having the manpower and resources to go into built up areas and, therefore, relying on the volunteer forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Dr. Gow, I would ask you now to watch the video sequence being part 2 of Exhibit 69, please. (Part 2 of Exhibit 69 was played) Could we stop that there for a moment, please? Is there not normally sound attached to this one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not believe there should be any sound attached, but if I could ask for it to be replayed for my benefit, I am afraid I was remiss and forgot to change monitors and so I was waiting for it to begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Could we take it back and start again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who is this that is being shown on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was Arkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Does he appear again there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He does.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who are the people that are in that circle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If we could go back, as you go through I will identify one person in particular.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps if it was played again, you might indicate to us the people there; could it be replayed again, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Would you like to tell us what you would hope to get out of this? To me it means nothing at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I might ask the witness to tell us the significance of it as it is being played. Can you tell us the significance of it and who it is that is appearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is again an extract from The Cook Report special. Here we see Arkan in his headquarters. The crest on the wall is that of his Serbian volunteer guard. So, if we can continue, please, thank you. As we move into the second sequence, the second sequence that we now see -- if you could let it run just a little further, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Could it go a little further, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You see Arkan himself there clearly identified on the left-hand side. Here, if you can stop at that point, this sequence is filmed in the town of Bijeljina in north eastern Bosnia at the time on April 2nd, I think it was, 1992, the day on which Arkan's forces had entered the town of Bijeljina as identified on documents I provided earlier. Arkan is here seen kissing a woman. That woman is Biljana Plavsic who at that time was one of the two Serbian representatives to the collective presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Immediately after this, Mrs. Plavsic and her corepresentative, Nikola Koljevic, were to resign and both of them are now acting or have been since then were acting as deputy presidents of the Serbian Republic in Bosnia and Herzegovina, after that the Republika Srpska, and Arkan again. Mrs. Plasvsic, I should point out, on this occasion is greeting and congratulating Arkan on the successful operation in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: To address His Honour's question, you refer to this to demonstrate a sense of co-operation between Arkan and the Republic of Srpska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do it to demonstrate, first of all, in response to one of the questions that was put earlier in the day, the presence of Arkan and his paramilitary forces on the territories of Bosnia and Herzegovina and, secondly, to indicate the co-operation that there was with senior political figures who would become part of the Republika Srpska administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. Dr. Gow, what tactics were employed against the non-Serbs by the JNA during the course of the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The forces either of the JNA or operating with the JNA in Bosnia and Herzegovina carried out a series of actions associated with political activities. The violent part of those activities involved a significant degree of terror widely reported in a number of areas in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I would ask you to look at the map that I now show you. (Handed). What is that a map of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a map of reported sites of camps in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Do you want to me to -----

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who prepared the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The map was prepared by the Office of the Prosecutor at my direction on information derived from United Nations documentation. I believe the map is selective rather than exclusive. For example, it does not include any reference to camps that might have been organised by either Croat or, I believe, reference to camps that might have been organised by either Croat or Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I tender that, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 71 will be admitted. MR. NIEMANN (To the witness): Might that Exhibit 71 be placed on the overhead projector? I think you have already answered part of this. This map relates to camps that were established?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It does indeed. If I might explain, that as the crisis, as the combined JNA, post JNA and paramilitary armed forces were active with the associated political programmes, in a number of areas a process of separation of the population began. There were widespread reports of extensive use of violence in a number of areas, allegations of atrocities and, in a number of cases, many number of cases, there was a process by which if people were not killed they were then administratively processed, separated into military, potentially military age males and others. They were in many cases given the opportunity to leave through administrative processes on the basis of paying for exit visas and for transportation, and on the basis of signing over property and other assets to the authorities of the newly designated Republika Srpska which, I might add, from day one had all its official documentation in place, including all the rubber stamps and letter headed paper. As part of this process, a number of camps were established, conventionally referred to as "concentration camps", a term which causes some concern, I think for the most part relates specifically to the literal sense of the word in which people are concentrated in one area for security purposes, otherwise detention centres. These were created in a number of areas, as you can see, throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. Dr. Gow, would you go to page 71 of Exhibit 30 being the book by General Kadijevic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Dr. Gow, could you look at the map again, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would be happy to, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I see Omarska appears there, Trnopolje appears there, where is the Keraterm camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe Keraterm, as far as I am able to establish, is somewhere there, but I am not sure exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If your Honour pleases, we will be calling evidence of the precise location of Keraterm during the course of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It is not on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I may ask the witness to mark it on the map where he located Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I do object to it on the basis, your Honour, that the witness has already -- as long as it is indicated on the basis that the witness has some uncertainty about it.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Does he? Let me ask you this. This is Exhibit 71. This is listed and it was admitted as a map of location of reported Serb camps in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Does this purport to show all of the detention camps operated by Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I believe when I began talking about the map I clearly indicated I regarded it as selected identification of camps. It was by no means intended to convey any sense of being exhaustive, and I believe I made that clear when I began.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You did; you said it did not include camps operated by groups other than Serbs -- at least, that was my understanding. I thought you said Croats.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did indeed -- I did say, for example, that it did not include reference to any of the camps that might have been operated by Croats and Muslims, but it still made it selective and I would not necessarily regard it as being comprehensive in terms of camps operated on the part of the Serbian political and military bodies either. I would also stress with regard to the request that was made I did indicate uncertainty. As far as I understand it, Keraterm (from the little that I know about Keraterm specifically) was a ceramics factory and where the exact location of this place is, I am afraid I would have considerable uncertainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So you do not know where Keraterm is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not -- I do not know where it is. I have an approximate idea, I thought.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Dr. Gow, perhaps that Exhibit might be given to the Registrar? Returning to page 71 of Exhibit 30, the English translation: Dr. Gow, do you wish to draw our attention to something that appears on that page in relation to your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would draw your attention to the section here in this main paragraph and would, in particular, draw your attention to the view of General Kadijevic and the command of the JNA, a decision which was made in conjunction with representatives of the Republic of Serbia to the SFRY presidency, that in the process of the dissolution of the SFRY that, as a priority at the political level, in addition to any military operations, they had to mount a counter offensive which would confront the destroyers of the old Yugoslavia, that is, those who would become independent, with a new Yugoslavia composed of those peoples who wanted to live together in it and who would not allow the disintegration of such a Yugoslavia. This, I think, is significant in placing the evidence I have been giving over the past couple of days in an overall context. The General is clearly identifying the political project to create new territorial entities. The reference to peoples would be loyal to it maybe, in the General's interpretation, might include non-Serbs but, from other parts of his text and certainly from what happened in practice, was primarily designed to include Serbian peoples and to be for those Serbian peoples; and that this was a project which extended through parts of the territory of Croatia and parts of the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and that that was the context in which all the other things which we have been discussing has to be considered.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Dr. Gow, you said in the course of your evidence that the JNA left air force units in Bosnia. In addition to the aircrafts themselves, were air crews left in Bosnia as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, some air crew were left in Bosnia and some air crew and aircraft were left in the Republic of Serbian Krajina. However, it might be significant to point out, for example, that in February 1994 the shadow of the JNA, the three elements of the air force all acted together in an operation against targets in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The pilots were supplied from the Vojska Yugoslavia air base at Podgorica in Montenegro. They were transferred to Udvina air base in the Serbian Krajina area, and from there they flew operations on behalf of the Bosnian Serbs against targets in Bosnia and Herzegovina. This indicates, I think, the degree to which reference to the political project and political military project I have just described throughout the period there was a significant degree of co-ordination and in one sense, although the JNA in one sense had bequeathed what would formally be three armies, to a large extent, they could still act and would still act as one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did the military aircraft that was left behind in Bosnia include fixed wing aircraft as well as helicopter aircraft.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It did yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you have anything more of Arkan to play or have you decided not to play that, the interview?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: There is one thing.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It is in evidence; it is up to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We have played all of the tapes that I would wish to play, your Honour, but there is one thing I just needed to attend to. I could not attend to it yesterday because the exhibits were not here, but could Exhibit 10(A) be shown to the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 16?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: 10A, your Honour, I am sorry. It is a map. (Handed). (To the witness): Dr. Gow, could you place that on the overhead projector so we can just see? I think you said earlier in your evidence in answer to one of her Honour's questions that you may have made a mistake when you made those notations on that map; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is indeed correct. As I was speaking to her Honour, the judge, it flashed into my mind that I had written these two things down the wrong way round. So I would just wish to correct the markings on the map, that where it says "after 1878" it should be "to 1878" and vice-versa.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So you want to change the "to" and the "after"?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you have any objection or do you want another exhibit to come in as a correction, Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Let me just confer for a second. We have no problem here.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. The witness then may correct the exhibit, I guess, and mark it according to your understanding now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps it could be shown to us again with the corrections that you have made? Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I have two, I think, short questions. I do not know if the witness is going to be here tomorrow morning, whether I can ask them then or now?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: He will be here for cross-examination tomorrow, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: As I indicated yesterday, we will be adjourning early today. So we will adjourn until 10 a.m. tomorrow morning. (The hearing was adjourned) 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: (The hearing adjourned for a short time)
